findings.title: Stale 'machinery removal' phrasing survives in five package spots and contradicts the revised extraction design
findings.detail: Revision 2 correctly replaces deletion with extraction everywhere operative (requirement (c), plannedItems feed-scroll.ts item, plan.md 'Scroll-memory extraction' section, AC statements, developer-overview boundaries), but grep over the package still finds 'machinery removal'/'scroll-machinery removal'/'dead scroll-machinery removal' in: plan.manifest.json:53 (REQ-FE-MESSENGER-SURFACE description opening — 'the attachment mapping seam, the modal focus handlers and the scroll-machinery removal all live in messenger.ts', while item (c) of the same requirement correctly says extraction), plan.manifest.json:338 (AC-FE-MESSENGER-SURFACE title 'Attachment lists + modal focus + machinery removal proven by mocha' — the AC statement at :346 is correct), plan.manifest.json:421 (finalAuditGates line '...modal focus + machinery removal — mocha, verify green'), plan.md:53 (workstream preamble), developer-overview.md:81 (execution model). plan-review-request.md:21 carries the same stale phrase but is the round-1 request artifact. Risk: the final auditor keying on the finalAuditGates line or the AC title would verify 'removal' the plan deliberately does not do (the Messenger preserve path must STAY); the one-owner rationale itself remains valid since the extraction, the focus handlers and the mapping seam all still live in messenger.ts.
findings.requiredFix: Not blocking. Reword the five spots to 'scroll-memory extraction' (e.g. AC title 'Attachment lists + modal focus + scroll-memory extraction proven by mocha'; finalAuditGates '+ scroll-memory extraction'; preamble 'the scroll-memory extraction'). Acceptable as a verified freeze-bookkeeping fold-in exactly like the 2026-11-01-email-search F-1 fold-in; the reviewer must re-check the delta edit-by-edit and re-hash at freeze.

findings.title: 'Disjoint triggers, never fight' safety claim is imprecise: store emits also fire Messenger CDU on undestroyed former instances, safe only under per-caller plan execution
findings.detail: plan.md WS-FE-FEED-SCROLL item 1 ('the Messenger-internal preserve plans ... never fight the page engine (disjoint triggers, one memory)'), developer-overview and the AC-FE-FEED-SCROLL statement repeat the same justification. The conclusion is correct but the mechanism is incomplete: triggers are NOT fully disjoint — hbs-children are replaced by every page re-render WITHOUT destroy() (documented at chat.ts:12-16), so every former Messenger instance keeps its live withStore subscription and its storeHandler fires setProps -> CDU -> plan request on EVERY store emit, alongside the page engine's plan. These zombie plans are harmless only because plan execution is per-caller: today's planMessagesScroll resolves this.element?.querySelector('.messenger__container') (messenger.ts:337), which for a detached instance is a detached node. If the extracted 'coalesced plan helper' were implemented as a module-global single slot (one plan per frame across all callers) and/or resolved the target via document.querySelector, a zombie's late 'preserve' request could displace the page engine's plan on the live container — the divergence case being a pending typing-placeholder tail while the reader is unpinned (page plans bottom, zombie preserve restores top; all other store-emit cases coincide: no-growth -> restore memory top, append-pinned -> bottom, prepend-unpinned -> top, chat-change -> bottom+memory delete). The plan's own constraints already imply the safe shape ('messenger.ts sources all of it ... zero behavior change; the Messenger CDU preserve path stays byte-for-byte in effect' = per-instance semantics; the page plan is 'applied to the live .messenger__container' by the page), and the chat.test.ts decision table drives the REAL page whose re-renders create real subscribing Messenger children, so a global-slot misimplementation turns the pending-tail decision red — hence minor, not major.
findings.requiredFix: Not blocking. Pin the helper contract in plan.md WS-FE-MESSENGER item (feed-scroll.ts): the module owns the shared per-chat memory, the one-time document-capture installScrollSync and the plan-RESOLUTION logic; each caller keeps its own rAF coalescing and applies its plan to its OWN element (page -> its live .messenger__container, Messenger -> this.element), never document-resolved — with one sentence noting that store-driven Messenger plans land on detached former instances and must never be able to displace the page engine's plan.

implementationQuality.summary: The extraction design is sound and the round-1 regression risk is gone: feed-scroll.ts (shared per-chat memory + one-time document-capture sync + plan helper) is created in WS-FE-MESSENGER with zero Messenger behavior change, and WS-FE-FEED-SCROLL's store-driven engine consumes the same module (pages->components is a legal downward import; precedent contacts.ts:13 imports components/messenger/messenger.ts), so both writers share one memory instead of racing two maps. Collision analysis for check (1): a store emit and a Messenger-internal setProps cannot interleave within one task (single-threaded JS); when both schedule plans in one frame, both resolve against the one shared memory and agree in every combination (preserve respects memory.pinned, restore-top restores memory.top for pinned and unpinned readers alike; chat-change detaches the old Messenger before its rAF lands) — the only divergent path is the zombie-interference case pinned as F-5, which the decision-table tests exercise through the real page. Ownership unchanged and clean: feed-scroll.ts appears only in WS-FE-MESSENGER writes (not readOnly anywhere; dependsOn expresses sequencing), write-sets remain pairwise disjoint across all three workstreams, wave-1 pair shares no file, forbiddenWrites unchanged, docs last-wave-only, WS-FE-SETTINGS-MOBILE untouched.
